subject: Performance SLO / Private VPC - network & VPN qualification
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@acme.com>, Sofia Morales <sofia.morales@acme.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 24 Mar 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: Performance SLOs + Private/VPC qualification

Thanks for the time today - good sync. Quick recap and next steps so we have a shared checklist:

Key performance targets you mentioned:
- Latency: p95 end-to-end (app -> Redwood private endpoint -> model) target <= 120 ms for streaming responses (token-by-token streaming).
- Throughput: sustained 200 requests/sec with bursts to 400 req/sec for short periods.
- Concurrency: expected concurrency up to ~50 active sessions during peak windows.
- Streaming: need support for low-latency chunked responses (server-sent events / gRPC streaming) and client-side partial renders.

Private/VPC deployment notes we covered:
- Preferred connectivity: VPC Peering (direct) to our dedicated VPC in us-west-2.
- Alternative: IPSec VPN tunnel if peering not possible.
- Egress: we need to confirm whether you NAT egress or have dedicated egress IP ranges that we can whitelist.
- Internal latency budget: your app/backend -> Redwood edge should be < 30 ms for internal processing to meet the 120 ms p95 end-to-end.

Info/asks from our side (next steps):
1) Please share Acme network diagram and egress IP ranges (David - attaching current diagram would help).
2) Confirm whether you can accept VPC Peering to our account in us-west-2 or if you need a VPN tunnel. If VPN, please share preferred terminate points.
3) Provide a point-of-contact for network tests (traceroute/iperf/http streaming).
4) We'll provision a temporary test endpoint (dedicated test VPC) for iperf/traceroute and an HTTP streaming sandbox - Jordan will own the deep technical dive.

Attached: redwood_private_vpc_requirements.pdf (high-level checklist).

Proposed scheduling: Jordan and I are available for a 60-minute technical deep-dive on Friday 3/26 or Monday 3/29 - what works for your team?

Thanks - Marissa

--

From: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Sofia Morales <sofia.morales@acme.com>, David Li <david.li@acme.com>
Date: Wed, 24 Mar 2027 17:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Performance SLOs + Private/VPC qualification

Hi Marissa - thanks for the summary and for the checklist. A few quick answers from our side and I've attached the network diagram (acme_network_diagram.png):

- We can commit to trying VPC Peering first; we have peering available to partners but need to check with infra for permissions.
- Current egress: our app VPC NATs through a set of Elastic IPs (10.1.254.0/27 mapped to public EIPs). I'll get the exact ranges from David.
- RTT observations: our service in us-west-2 typically sees ~10-16 ms RTT to AWS peers in the same region; within our DCs internal hops are sub-5 ms.
- Ports: we can open outbound TCP 443 and 1194 (if using IPSec), and can create Security Group rules to allow testing from Redwood test IPs.

Network contact: David Li (david.li@acme.com) - he's copied here and will own the packet-level tests and diagram details.

We're comfortable with the proposed targets but want to validate with a short load test/streaming trial before committing the SLA. Friday 3/26 10:00 PT works for a first pass.

- Tom

Date: Thu, 25 Mar 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Performance SLOs + Private/VPC qualification

Thanks Tom and David - that's helpful. Quick follow-up and technical asks so the Friday deep-dive is productive:

1) David - can you share the exact EIP ranges and the Security Group rules that control outbound egress? If you can provide a short-lived credentialed traceroute/iperf endpoint we can consume for one-hour tests that would speed validation.
2) Tests we recommend (we'll provide a test checklist):
   - Traceroute & MTR from your app host to our test IPs (for path and hop latency)
   - iperf3 (TCP) for baseline throughput and jitter (15-60s runs at increasing parallel streams)
   - HTTP/1.1 chunked streaming and gRPC streaming tests with ~2-4 KB token chunks to validate token-by-token latency under load
   - A short synthetic load to reproduce 200 req/s sustained at 50 concurrent sessions (we can coordinate a 10-15 minute window)

3) Peering vs VPN: if you can enable peering that will give the lowest variability. If not, VPN is fine - please share proposed endpoints and whether you prefer route-based or policy-based tunnels.

4) Whitelisting: please plan to whitelist two test EIPs we'll provide. For production we'll coordinate on permanent egress ranges or private peering.

Jordan and I will prepare a proposed test plan + temporary test VPC and send it before the call. We'll also add a mutual action plan to the HubSpot deal and include the test checklist.

See you Friday 3/26 at 10:00 PT - calendar invite forthcoming.

Best,
Marissa

Subject: Internal: ACME - action items after network qualification call

Jordan - quick internal note after the Friday deep-dive (summarized for your action items):

- Owner: Jordan to run the technical deep-dive and own the test endpoint provisioning (temporary test VPC in us-west-2).
- Tasks:
  1) Create a shared test plan doc (we have a template) and upload to the HubSpot deal (ACME-2027-0345). Link: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1a2b3c-example
  2) Provide two test EIPs for David to whitelist and a short list of TCP ports (443, 1194) for the trial.
  3) Coordinate a 15-min smoke test and a 15-min full load at 200 req/s. Collect p50/p95/p99 and token-by-token latency traces.
  4) Note any network jitter or retransmits - include those in the post-test perf report.
- Timeline: aim to have test env ready by EOD Tue 3/30 and run tests Wed 3/31.

I've added the mutual action plan in HubSpot and assigned preliminary tasks - please update ownership as you confirm times with Acme.

Thanks - Marissa
